title: 30-Minute Pivot
teaches: The 30-minute pivot as we trade it: an entry timer on 30-minute bars for a daily long setup at a level, in a leader above its 50-day and 200-day with a rising 20-day EMA; a string of red 30-minute candles into the level, then the first green 30-minute candle, the pivot; the buy is a cent over its high at market, never more than 4% past it; the stop sits a few cents under a low, 1-3% preferred, 3.5% good, up to 5%, and past 5% we wait for a tighter trigger; the 40% position cap sets the size on tight stops; the first sell is a judgment, usually day 3 or later into a 3, 5 or 7 day push, with the rest on the trail; a loss at the stop is the plan working.

facts.quote: a tactical entry method designed to help traders buy high momentum stocks at defined support levels while minimizing the risk of "chasing" a move.
facts.claim: The originator calls it a tactical entry method for buying strong stocks at support without chasing.

facts.quote: The strategy focuses on "RS names" stocks that are holding up better than the broad market.
facts.claim: The originator uses it on RS names, stocks holding up better than the market.

facts.quote: A key signal for this entry is seeing a string of red 30-minute candles in a stock that is otherwise in a strong uptrend.
facts.claim: The originator's signal: a string of red 30-minute candles in a stock in a strong uptrend.

facts.quote: Rather than buying as the stock is falling, the trader waits for a "pivot" a specific point where the downward momentum on the 30minute chart shifts back to the upside.
facts.claim: The originator waits for the 30-minute chart to turn back up instead of buying the fall.

facts.quote: By entering at the 30 minute pivot, you have a defined spot for a stop loss, usually just below the recent 30 minute low.
facts.claim: The originator's stop: usually just below the recent 30-minute low.

facts.quote: It seeks to buy the "dip" in a leading stock, often near short term support levels like the 8 EMA
facts.claim: The originator buys the dip in a leader, often near a short-term average.

facts.quote: I find during periods of volatility it can pretty hard to hold a position. That's why I developed my 30 min pivot strategy.
facts.claim: The originator built the 30-minute pivot for volatile markets, when a position is hard to hold.

facts.quote: I buy weakness after strength and use the 30 min pivot to make it happen. Here's another example with the trade now over 10R. My price 102.99
facts.claim: HOOD: the originator bought weakness after strength with the pivot at 102.99; the trade went over 10R.

facts.quote: 30-min pivot is my goto for tight risk in leading names.
facts.claim: The originator uses it for tight risk in leading names.

facts.quote: When the price touches the 20 period moving average, put a buy stop above the high of the previous bar.
facts.claim: Raschke's Holy Grail: at the 20-period average, a buy stop above the prior bar's high.

facts.quote: Once filled, enter a protective sell stop at the newly formed swing low. Trail stops as profits grow.
facts.claim: Raschke: the stop goes at the new swing low, then trails.

facts.quote: Stop is always lows of the day and stop should not be wider than the ATR or ADR of the stock
facts.claim: Kullamagi: the stop should not be wider than the stock's ATR or ADR.

facts.quote: Entry is opening range highs or the first green 5-minute candle or any range break to the upside
facts.claim: Kullamagi's parabolic long buys the first green 5-minute candle, the same idea on another bar.

facts.quote: Pivot Points use the prior period's high, low, and close to estimate future support and resistance levels.
facts.claim: ChartSchool: floor-trader pivot points are levels computed from the prior period's high, low and close.

facts.quote: Pivot Points for 30-, 60-, and 120-minute charts use the prior week's high, low, and close.
facts.claim: ChartSchool: on 30-minute charts those pivot points come from the prior week's prices.

facts.claim: GLW: our Sunday Scans flagged a 30-minute pivot off the 20-day EMA.

facts.claim: TEAM: an undercut of the range that closes with a strong lower wick.

facts.quote: Stop first (by default a few cents under the day's low or the prior day's low, F62); the size comes from the stop; if the honest stop does not fit the risk, skip the trade.
facts.claim: A3: stop first; the size comes from the stop; if the honest stop does not fit, skip.

facts.quote: The stop is the exit. It only moves up, never down or wider. The one exception is the gap rule (B20).
facts.claim: A4: the stop is the exit; it only moves up; the gap rule is the one exception.

facts.quote: Shares = account × risk % ÷ (entry − stop), rounded down, then capped: the size is the SMALLER of the risk-based size and the position cap

facts.quote: With a ceiling: if the first 30 minutes take the loss past 2R, get out.
facts.claim: B20's ceiling: if the first 30 minutes take the loss past 2R, get out.

facts.claim: C28: never buy more than 4% above the buy point.

facts.claim: Later sells are a judgment: sell more into strength on a later push, and trail what is left.

walkthroughs.title: DK, August 2026: the textbook pivot
steps: DK, August 24, 2026, on the 30-minute chart. A leader sells off all morning, 6 red candles from 9:30 to 12:00.
The selling lands on its rising daily average, 66.48. The 12:30 candle turns green off 66.08 and closes on its high.
That green candle is your pivot. The 13:00 candle takes its high: buy at market, 66.83. Stop 66.05, 1.17% away.
A trade under 66.08 and it's wrong. It held. 3R in 6 bars, same day. Stop to breakeven, no sell yet.

walkthroughs.title: DOCU, October 2026: the shake at the 21-day

walkthroughs.title: PSX, August 2026: when the cap sets the size
steps: A quiet pullback in PSX, August 27, 2026: 5 red 30-minute candles down onto its rising daily average, 236.78.

questions.q: Which candle is your pivot?
choices: The green one that just closed
The first candle of the day
The next green one after it
Any green candle at the average
questions.answer: The green one that just closed
questions.why: The green one that just closed. It's the first green 30-minute candle after the string of reds, and it's sitting right on the level. Green means it closed above its open. The reds were sellers leaning on it all morning. This candle is the first sign buyers showed up at the average. You don't buy the fall. You wait for this turn, and then its high becomes your trigger.
questions.lesson_line: Reds into the level, then the first green candle. That's your pivot.

wrong.The first candle of the day: That's the opening range, a different trade that buys the 9:30 to 10:00 high. Here the opening candle was still red, still selling.
wrong.The next green one after it: Late. The turn is the first green candle. Wait for a second one and you've given up the tight stop the pivot is built for.
wrong.Any green candle at the average: Only the first green one after a red string counts. Call any green candle a pivot and you end up buying noise.

questions.simple: Your pivot is the first green candle after the reds, at the level. That's where the selling turns.

reasons: +2 the unit stands on D-002, the turn candle at support

questions.story: Four red 30-minute candles, from yesterday's last half hour into this morning. They run down to a rising daily average. The last candle on the screen just closed green.

questions.q: The 30-minute pivot doesn't find you stocks. The daily chart picks the stock and the level, and the pivot times the buy.
questions.why: True. The daily chart does the picking: a leader, pulled back to a level like the rising 20-day EMA. Then you drop to the 30-minute chart to pick the moment. ChartMaster, who built it, calls it an entry method for buying strong stocks at support without chasing. That's how I use it. I flagged GLW at the 30 min pivot off the 20EMA.
questions.lesson_line: The daily chart picks the stock and the level. The 30-minute pivot times the buy.
questions.simple: True, the daily chart picks the stock and the level. The pivot only picks the moment to buy.

reasons: +2 the unit stands on D-002, which setup the name means

questions.q: Where do you buy it?
choices: A cent over that green candle's high
A cent over the 9:30 to 10:00 high
On the close of the green candle
At the average, with a limit order
questions.answer: A cent over that green candle's high
questions.why: A cent over the green candle's high, once a later candle trades through it. That high is your trigger. A trade through it shows buyers will pay more than they did at the turn, after the sellers had their shot. Buy it at market as it trades, in regular hours. Here the 10:30 candle took it, and the buy filled at 106.65. Your stop goes a few cents under the green candle's low.
questions.lesson_line: The pivot candle's high is the line. A trade through it is your buy.

wrong.A cent over the 9:30 to 10:00 high: That's the opening range breakout's line. The pivot's line is the turn candle's high, often well under the morning high.
wrong.On the close of the green candle: The close shows you the turn. It doesn't prove it. You wait for a later candle to take the high.
wrong.At the average, with a limit order: That's buying the fall and hoping the line holds. We wait for the turn, then buy through it at market.

questions.simple: You buy a cent over the green candle's high, when a later candle trades through it.

reasons: the trigger line is shared by both options of the held decision D-127
the card line is a proposed criterion

questions.story: A leader sells off on the 30-minute chart into its rising daily average. The 9:30 candle is red. The 10:00 candle turns and closes green.

questions.q: On a pivot you may buy while the red string is still falling, before the green candle closes.
questions.why: False. No buying while the red string is still falling. The green candle must close first, and then a later candle must trade a cent over its high. The originator waits for the pivot instead of buying the fall.
questions.lesson_line: Let the green candle close. Then let a later candle take its high.
questions.simple: False. Wait for the green candle to close first, because buying while the stock still falls is buying too early.

reasons: the card line and the originator's words agree

questions.q: The stock closed under its 200-day yesterday. Today a clean 30-minute pivot forms at the 20-day EMA. Do you take it?
choices: No, it's under the 200-day
No, we never buy before 10:30
Yes, a clean pivot beats the line
Yes, the 20-day EMA is still rising
questions.why: No. Under the 200-day we don't buy stocks. That's a hard line, and no candle changes it. The only exception is an index or a levered ETF, on a reversal extension or a parabolic long. This one's a plain stock. Under the 200-day the big trend is down, and those aren't the dips we buy. Wait for it to get back over the line.
questions.lesson_line: Under the 200-day there's no pivot long to take. Wait for the line.

wrong.No, we never buy before 10:30: We don't have a time-of-day rule. The reason to pass is the 200-day.
wrong.Yes, a clean pivot beats the line: No candle beats the 200-day. For a stock it's a hard rule.
wrong.Yes, the 20-day EMA is still rising: A rising 20-day is nice. It doesn't move the 200-day line, and that line says no.

questions.simple: Pass. We don't buy stocks under the 200-day, however clean the candles look.

reasons: +3 one cited fact, the 200-day rule (B26)
+2 rests on the owner's rulebook

questions.q: You use the 30-minute pivot on leaders: stocks with an RS rating of 80 or better, in one of the strongest groups.
questions.why: True. The pivot is a timer, so it's only as good as the stock you point it at. We buy leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in the strongest groups. RS, relative strength, shows you which names are holding up better than the market. ChartMaster calls them RS names. Our RS Rating puts that number right on the chart.
questions.lesson_line: The timer is only as good as the stock. Leaders first.
questions.simple: True. The pivot times the buy, so point it at leaders with an RS rating of 80 or more.
